Title: Acta et scripta theologorum Wirtembergensium et Patriarchae Constantinopolitani D. Hieremiae, quae utrique ab anno MDLXXVI usque ad annum MDLXXXI de Augustana Confessione inter se miserunt, Graece et Latine ab iisdem theologis edita
Creator: Wirtemberg (Tubingen) theologians (the catalogue names Jacob Andreae and Martin Crusius) and Jeremias II, Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople (the catalogue names him Jeremias II; the title page says D. Hieremiae); the correspondence over the Augsburg Confession, 1576-1581, published in 1584 by the theologians
Publisher: Wittenberg: Officina Haeredum Johannis Cratonis, 1584 (title page: Witebergae ... M.D.LXXXIIII; the Bavarian State Library's own catalogue record reads the same year)
Publication Date: 1584
Rights: Public Domain (pre-1930 publication); the item description records the Bavarian State Library (MDZ) as the source and gives no reuse statement
Language: lat (Latin only in this file: the title page says Greek and Latin, but the OCR contains no Greek-script characters, so the Greek columns are not recovered)
Source: Internet Archive item acta-et-scripta-theologorum-wirtembergensium-17608947098888bsb-10150005, full-text OCR file Acta et scripta theologorum Wirtembergensium17608947098888bsb10150005_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the library/source-research thread, 2026-09-29. The item page carries no possible-copyright-status or licence field; the description says the scan is from the Bavarian State Library (Digitale Sammlungen, bsb10150005). This thread did not consult MDZ's own reuse statement.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the library thread; the OCR text follows unchanged, apart from this header. Rights basis: the 1584 publication date, more than 95 years before 2026, clears this registry's public-domain-by-date rule. INTAKE section 2 asks that MDZ's own reuse statement be checked for a scan from that library; it was not available in the item record, so the rights basis here is the print date only. OCR artifacts are left as found; nothing was corrected, re-spaced or retyped.
Content note: The Greek column is garbled beyond use (no Greek characters survive); the Latin is usable, though with long-s and column-layout errors. This is a mixed volume. It opens with the theologians' Latin prefaces, letters and the Augsburg Confession; the body then runs in three rounds, each headed by the Patriarch's reply (running heads 'Primum / Secundum / Tertium Patriarchae Responsum') with the theologians' answering text ('Responsum ad primum ...') alternating with it. Only the Patriarch's portions are his church's voice, and what survives here is the Latin the theologians printed, not the Patriarch's Greek. The theologians' portions are a Lutheran party's outside voice.
